books.section: Topic 4.4 America on the World Stage, A. Trade, Diplomacy, and the Expansion of American Influence

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of the report of the Hartford Convention, January 1815: In December 1814, as diplomats negotiated an end to the War of 1812, Federalist delegates from New England met at Hartford, Connecticut, to protest the war and the power of the Democratic-Republican government. A few radical delegates talked of New England leaving the Union, but the convention rejected secession. Instead it proposed amendments to the Constitution, including requiring a two-thirds vote of Congress to declare war, to admit new states, or to restrict trade, and barring two presidents in a row from the same state. The convention sent delegates to Washington to present its demands, and arrived just as news came that the war had ended.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Report of the Hartford Convention, January 1815. Paraphrased, not quoted; public domain source.

source: original; stimulus as described in the stimulus source note

options.text: after the War of 1812 had ended in victory
options.misconception: It met in December 1814, while the war was still on.

options.text: during the War of 1812, while peace was being negotiated
before the United States declared war on Britain
options.misconception: War was declared in June 1812, two and a half years earlier.

options.text: after the Monroe Doctrine was announced
options.misconception: The Doctrine came in 1823, eight years later.

rationales.A: The convention met in December 1814, and the war did not end until the Treaty of Ghent, signed later that month and ratified in 1815.
rationales.B: The passage says the delegates met in December 1814 “as diplomats negotiated an end to the War of 1812.” The war was still on.
rationales.C: Congress declared war in June 1812. The convention met two and a half years later, near the war's end.
rationales.D: The Monroe Doctrine was announced in December 1823, eight years after Hartford. It cannot frame a meeting from 1814.
rationales.general:
1. Read the first line. The delegates met in December 1814, “as diplomats negotiated an end to the War of 1812.”
2. Ask what that means. Negotiating an end means the war was still going.
3. Put it together. The convention met during the war, not after it.
Background: The Federalists met because New England merchants had lost their trade with Britain during the war.
Remember: when a passage says delegates met while peace was negotiated, the war was still on.
